parallel.requirements: Recognized ESM, .mjs output, no npm dependencies, manual argv parity, Python int/string formatting, ASCII encode, and bencode encode/decode; the workflow also pursued extra edge cases such as Unicode digits, help text, and scale.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent owned implementation and launched one workflow with eight verifier dimensions plus planned triage/review/critic phases; children owned fuzzing, not final code integration.
parallel.implementation: Parent wrote /output/test6.mjs and library modules for argparse, Python-like bytes/errors/repr/numbers, Unicode properties, and bencode, then fixed the Nd run bug after local discovery.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Artifact validation found a complete /output tree with test6.mjs and libraries, but the final response was empty because the parent process timed out.
parallel.verification: Parent ran sampled differential cases and Nd checks; children found additional real divergences, especially CPython max digit limit behavior, but the killed workflow returned no aggregate result.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed 161/172, process_ok=false, workflow status killed/result null, and child-discovered divergences were not integrated before closure.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Node ESM, .mjs, manual argparse, exact output, bencode, ASCII encoding, and no external dependency requirements from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single agent handled probing, implementation, local differential test generation, cleanup, and the final response without delegation.
serial.implementation: Built a modular /output tree under lib/pytypes, lib/bencode, and lib/cli with BigInt int handling, bytes/repr support, bencode codec, and manual argparse.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Artifact validation found test6.mjs and the library tree, scratch harnesses were removed, and final.txt describes the delivered structure and verification.
serial.verification: Ran samples, a 71-case differential suite, and 300 plus 120 randomized cases before finalizing; these local checks missed the same official failing surface.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation also failed 161/172, apparently from ordinary behavioral gaps such as CPython max digit rejection not covered by the local tests; process completed normally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the Python source, Node ESM output, exact argv behavior, bencode encode/decode, ASCII encode, and no external dependency constraints, then over-expanded verification into additional edge-case obligations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same core porting obligations from the prompt and explicitly delivered a module tree covering Python bytes, int parsing, repr, bencode, and argparse behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No official requirement was unique to one run, but parallel pursued a broader verifier-generated behavioral surface while serial kept the accepted task interpretation inside one trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent implemented the port, then delegated eight verification dimensions to workflow children with triage and review phases planned after fuzzing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had no delegation and the same actor handled probing, implementation, local tests, cleanup, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split verification broadly across children while retaining implementation ownership; serial avoided cross-agent lifecycle overhead.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow brief gave children a shared harness and per-dimension prompts, but the parent kept editing /output while children tested and no aggregate handoff returned.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial carried all observations and implementation state in the main trajectory, so findings from local checks were immediately available for subsequent edits.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit child briefs but no completed parent-facing verifier handoff; serial had continuous local context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a multi-module implementation using lib/unicode, lib/python, lib/bencode, lib/argparse, and /output/test6.mjs, then fixed the Nd digit-value bug during verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a different multi-module implementation under lib/pytypes, lib/bencode, and lib/cli, with BigInt-based int conversion and manual bencode/argparse support.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementations are structurally different, but both preserved arbitrary BigInt parsing without CPython 3.12 max digit rejection and therefore reached the same official score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The verifier workflow remained killed with result=null, several children stayed in progress or start state, and the parent process exited with timeout code 143.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run reached a normal process return code 0 and produced a final response explaining delivered files and checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the workflow result lifecycle at the coordination boundary, whereas serial completed its local result lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel artifact validation copied a complete /output tree, but verification children worked against a shared /output and /tmp while the parent was still changing code.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial artifact validation copied a complete /output tree, with scratch tests removed before closure and no child workspace sharing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both delivered artifacts, but parallel mixed live parent edits with concurrent verifier reads and temporary files while serial had a single coherent workspace owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed many local comparisons and verifier children found real divergences, including the long integer digit limit, but the workflow did not return for repair or final acceptance.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran 71 hand-picked differential cases plus randomized rounds and accepted the result locally before delivering a final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel discovered more relevant failing evidence than serial but failed to integrate it; serial verified less broadly and missed the same official failing surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full 2399 second agent budget with 26 workflow child logs and 711087 child tokens, leaving process_ok=false.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished in 840.464 seconds, left 1556 seconds in the cell budget, and process_ok=true.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel fan-out/retry verifier consumed the closure window, while serial closed normally despite the same official failure rate.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations failed with the same 161/172 score, so there is no discordant pass/fail outcome. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level: the serial run stayed single-agent, completed, and delivered a final response after local tests, while the parallel run implemented a similar port and launched a large verifier workflow. That workflow found additional real divergences, including Python rejecting integers above the CPython max digit threshold while the JS port accepted them, but repeated stalled retries and broad fan-out exhausted the remaining budget. The official result still matches serial because serial missed the same acceptance surface rather than solving it.
parallel_contributors: Implemented the port and an Nd fix, but exhausted budget in an eight-way verifier workflow with result=null and no final response.
Child verifier logs contain long-digit and argparse-space divergences that were not integrated before closure.
serial_contributors: Avoided workflow overhead, finished in 840.464 seconds, and produced a final response.
Its local 71-case and randomized checks did not include the CPython max digit rejection surface, so it also failed 161/172.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both solutions treat very large integer strings as BigInt values instead of enforcing CPython 3.12 max string digits, which is an ordinary behavioral porting defect rather than itself a concurrency label.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No official outcome difference; retained label is a realized adverse parallel process pattern, not an exclusive root cause of the shared failure.

The parent owned implementation, local checks, workflow launch, and delivery; the failure was budget exhaustion after verification fan-out, not an unowned pipeline.
Productive implementation began before the workflow; no mandatory serial preflight blocked implementation or assembly.
The run did not finish all investigation as a separate first phase before implementation; the broad investigation was a post-build verifier workflow.
The same closure problem is better classified as collective fan-out and retry budget exhaustion rather than auxiliary work starving one separate critical path.

The parent launched an eight-dimension verifier workflow after producing the port, the workflow repeatedly retried stalled children, and the run exhausted the 2400 second budget with the aggregate result still null. Concrete verifier findings, including the long-digit CPython limit mismatch, were therefore not returned and integrated before closure. The serial run did no fan-out and completed with a final response, but it independently missed the same acceptance surface, so this is an adverse parallel process pattern rather than an official outcome differential.
candidates.realized_consequence: The verifier workflow was killed with result=null after repeated stalled retries, leaving reported divergences unconsumed while the parent timed out and produced an empty final response.
candidates.near_match_reason: The absent verifier return is the downstream terminal state of the same excessive fan-out and retry budget exhaustion episode, so the load-imbalance label is the more specific retained boundary.
